title: Information Asymmetry and the Line Between Oversight and Management
summary: How boards manage the gap between what they know and what management knows, how decisions get made before the meeting, and where oversight ends and micromanagement begins.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: How boards manage the gap between what they know and what management knows, how decisions get made before the meeting, and where oversight ends and micromanagement begins.
Learning Objectives: Assess how the board validates information and uses independent assurance
Recognise when the board meeting has become a ratification exercise
Judge whether the board is under-engaged, appropriately engaged or micromanaging
Syllabus: Independent assurance: internal and external audit, risk function and outside experts
Pre-meetings and side conversations: legitimate preparation or foregone conclusion
Reading minutes for recorded debate and challenge
Oversight versus direction of day-to-day decisions and staff
Intended Audience: Supervisors and governance specialists who assess boards and senior management of regulated firms
Staff conducting fit and proper, governance or culture reviews and interviewing chairs and directors
Senior supervisors and team leaders who review governance assessments and decide the supervisory response
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of governance assessment or supervisory interviews is helpful. No board experience is required.
Core Reading: Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)
FSB, Guidance on Supervisory Interaction with Financial Institutions on Risk Culture (2014)
Amy C. Edmondson, The Fearless Organization: Creating Psychological Safety in the Workplace (2018)
